question: At gbrain d44296c (v0.60.30.0), is the shipped evidence default (auto: whole conversation pages within a 24,000-token conversation budget, other hits unchanged) non-inferior to the old chunk default on end-to-end answer accuracy, and is it better?

sealed.release_decision: the first of at most three release decisions the protocol allows; no earlier gbrain run has touched the set

candidate_commits.comparison_release: The same commit with return_unit chunk. At this commit the chunk unit skips evidence assembly and returns the ranked chunks unchanged, which is the pre-0.60.16 default. Both arms share one frozen retrieval, so only the delivered evidence differs.
candidate_commits.gbrain_evals_rule: The gbrain-evals commit containing this file; every answer file records this file's SHA-256 and the frozen evidence records the gbrain commit.

retrieval.frozen_once: One retrieval per question at the pinned commit, shared by both arms. A crashed freeze resumes per question; frozen questions are never re-retrieved.

arms.budget_note: No budget is passed, so gbrain's default applies (search.return_budget_conversation, 24,000 tokens for a trusted local caller). The answer step refuses any question whose applied budget differs.

reader.prompt: LongMemEval's chain-of-thought reading prompt (LME_READER_TEMPLATE in eval/runner/sealed-confirmation-lib.ts), the protocol's reader
reader.evidence_rendering: One dated pseudo-session per delivered block, the block text as a single turn, sorted by date (evidenceSessions in sealed-confirmation.ts). This is the shape the v2 solvability chunk oracle used. Both arms use it; only the delivered text differs.

judge.prompts: LongMemEval evaluate_qa.py per-kind prompts, abstention items with the unanswerable prompt (judgePrompt in sealed-confirmation-lib.ts)
judge.implementation: sealed-confirmation.ts score --judge, which verifies the labels commitment and appends an access-log line before parsing

metric.primary: answer_correct: the judge says yes. Denominator: all 200 questions (160 answerable plus 40 abstention). A reader error counts as incorrect.
exploratory: answer accuracy on the 160 answerable questions, and by question kind (80 multi-session, 40 temporal, 40 knowledge update, 40 abstention)
recall_all@5 and recall_any@5 over the 160 answerable questions (the shared retrieval; identical in both arms by construction)
mean provider-reported reader input tokens per arm; auto delivery counts (blocks delivered as pages, truncated, over budget)

rule.verdict: pass when compare.ts's non-inferiority comparison passes: the one-sided persona-cluster bootstrap p-value for delta <= -0.03 is at most 0.05 (equivalently the lower end of a 90% cluster-bootstrap interval for auto - chunk is above -3 points). fail when the whole 95% cluster-bootstrap interval lies below -0.03. inconclusive otherwise, when a comparison is blocked (missing or duplicated rows), or when either arm has more than max_reader_errors reader errors.
rule.superiority: Tested only after non-inferiority passes (fixed sequence, so no further alpha adjustment). confirmed when auto - chunk > 0 and both the exact two-sided McNemar p-value and the persona-clustered two-sided sign-flip p-value are below 0.05, the E2 rule of decision manifest v2. Otherwise not_confirmed.
rule.implementation: bun eval/runner/compare.ts with this family, then sealed-confirmation.ts decide (decideEvidence)

missing_and_errors.reader_retries: LlmClient retries each request up to four times. A crashed answer step is resumed by rerunning it on the same output file: answered questions are kept, and identical requests are served from the response cache, so nothing is re-sampled. At most three resume passes.
missing_and_errors.reader_error: After the resume passes, a question without an answer is judged incorrect and stays in the denominator.
missing_and_errors.missing_rows: A question missing from either arm blocks the comparison (inconclusive).
missing_and_errors.truncated_output: An answer stopped at 2,048 output tokens is judged as written.

label_reads: Labels are read twice, both through sealed-confirmation.ts score under this decision id: once for the chunk answers and once for the auto answers. No other label read is allowed.

budget.ledger: one eval/runner/budget-ledger.ts run (runner sealed-v2-decision-1) with --budget-usd 60, joined by every paid step; each reader and judge step also has its own LlmClient cap

no_second_try: Each arm is answered once. No other setting, budget, unit, reader or judge may be tried on the sealed set under this decision; a failed candidate is fixed on development data and re-preregistered as a new decision.
